name: IN-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Yakym has a massive fundraising advantage ($5.2M raised)
No polling or expert ratings; markets price Democrats at ~4%
model.rationale: The district's R+13 lean, Yakym's incumbency and overwhelming financial edge, and prediction markets near 97% Republican all point to a safe Republican hold. Democrat Jamee Decio's modest fundraising gives her little path to close a double-digit structural gap.
model.watch: A major late outside-spending intervention or unexpected incumbent misstep would be the only realistic route to making this competitive.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Indiana's second district is solidly Republican territory, and incumbent Rudy Yakym is seeking another term after easily retaining the seat in recent cycles. He has raised over $5.2 million and holds a large cash advantage, while Democrat Jamee Decio has raised about $356,000. No independent polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Yakym roughly a 97% chance of winning.

The forecast expects Yakym to win by a comfortable double-digit margin consistent with the district's partisan lean. A Libertarian candidate appears on the ballot but is not a significant factor. The main uncertainty is the exact size of the margin, not the winner.
